title: strength
description: Per-exercise progression plus monthly tonnage, each with the fact that qualifies it. Tonnage is VOLUME, not strength: it falls when pull work gives way to isolation whatever happened to capacity, so the figure that answers "am I getting stronger" is each repeated exercise's working weight over time. The engine publishes numbers only — whether a trend is good is the coach's sentence to write (ADR 0012).

exercises.description: One entry per exercise name the parsed sets contain, exact-name matched (Twisting Curl and Zottman Curl are distinct movements; nothing fuzzy), and a second entry for the same name when it was also done as a hold (an isometric set: a weight held still for a time), told apart by `measure`. Points are per DAY: the heaviest weight one rep moved (or one hold held) that day, and the day's summed kg·reps for the exercise — two numbers because when the weight drops and the reps rise, the product is the only one that says whether work went up.

top_reps.description: the most reps in one set that day

total_reps.description: the day's summed reps for the exercise, sets times reps

top_hold_s.description: the longest hold that day, in seconds; 0 on an entry whose measure is not "hold"

total_hold_s.description: the day's summed hold time for the exercise, sets times the seconds each was held; 0 on an entry whose measure is not "hold"

measure.description: what the exercise progresses in. "hold" for an entry of holds: its reps, total_reps and kg_reps are 0 (a hold adds no tonnage), top_kg is the heaviest weight held, and top_hold_s and total_hold_s are its progression. Otherwise "reps" when every point moved 0 kg, as a bodyweight exercise does (push ups, assisted chin ups and the like count 0 kg toward tonnage, imported or pasted) and as an imported set logged with no weight does: its top_kg and kg_reps are then 0, so top_reps and total_reps are its progression. "kg" when any point moved weight.

monthly.description: Every strength month from strength_coverage, INCLUDING the months the career spine refuses — a table can qualify a number where a curve cannot. `tonnage_known` is the both-possible flag (ADR 0009): false means the month sits under the coverage bar and no tonnage is claimed for it (kg is 0 there, an impossible-zero behind the flag), true means kg is the month's summed lifted mass. covered/total is the denominator that keeps a coverage shift from reading as a training trend.

sessions.description: The gaps themselves, made visible: with_sets parsed into rows; pasted_unparsed carried a non-empty description that yielded nothing (a format stride does not read — a different fact from never pasted); the remainder of total never had a paste to read. Deliberate omissions are omissions the report can name because these counts exist.
